title: Staged SDK compatibility rollout with telemetry gates and lean runtime deps
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Over the last two months we've observed subtle compatibility breakages across Python, JS and Go clients when downstream consumers use older transitive deps. Simultaneously, runtime memory and cold-start allocations have increased slightly due to redundant utility libraries in the clients. Goal: Perform a coordinated, staged dependency bump across all language clients, pruning non-essential runtime dependencies and gating releases with telemetry checks so we can hold back regressions without broad rollbacks. This ticket coordinates the engineering work, rollout gating, and automated health checks for the change wave.

Approach:
- Create a staged release plan per-client (python/js/go) with feature flags and canary channels.
- Replace or slim the biggest transitive runtime utilities (e.g., replace heavy JSON helper with small, focused serializer where safe).
- Introduce a compatibility test matrix in CI that runs against pinned older transitive versions to detect API surface assumptions.
- Add telemetry-based gates: release will only progress to the next stage if latency, error-rate, and token-cost metrics remain within pre-defined thresholds.
- Provide clear deprecation notes in client changelogs and a migration guide for customers relying on legacy fields.

Why this is different: Previous dep-bump work focused on monolithic lockfile regeneration; this effort prioritizes minimal runtime footprint, safe fallbacks, and automated holdback when telemetry indicates user-facing regressions.
acceptance_criteria: All three clients (python/js/go) released behind canary flags with bumped dependencies and passing compatibility matrix tests
Telemetry gates defined and wired: 99th p95 latency deviation <5%, error-rate delta <0.1% absolute, token-cost delta <2%
Migration guide published and changelog entries added for all clients
Roll-forward path documented and rollback playbook validated in staging
Benchmarks show <=5% median runtime increase and reduced cold-start allocations after pruning
steps: Inventory: list top-10 transitive deps by installed size and runtime allocations for each client
Prototype: swap heavy utility with lightweight alternative in python client and run microbenchmarks
CI: extend compatibility matrix to include oldest supported transitive versions and add smoke tests
Canary: publish canary packages + server-side canary toggle for 1% of traffic
Telemetry: implement dashboard and automated gate job that blocks promotion if thresholds violated
Rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% spaced 24h apart with automated checks at each step
Post-mortem: collect regressions, customer reports, and follow-up refactors
risks: Hidden API assumptions in customer code causing subtle breakage despite tests
Telemetry noise during traffic fluctuations could false-block a healthy rollout
Performance regressions due to new versions of low-level libs on certain CPU/GPU instance types
Packaging/asset issues for the Go module proxy causing failed installs in restricted networks
testing: Compatibility matrix run in CI covering N-2 transitive versions for each critical dep
Synthetic load tests in staging that simulate token distribution and request sizes
Canary A/B metrics compare user-observed latency and generated tokens cost to control group
Manual verification checklist for SDK maintainers before promoting to next stage
